Subject: POC MAP & environment needs (API keys, org, allowlist, peering)

Hi Rafael / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Luma is excited to move to a short POC to validate latency/cost for our recommendation pipeline. To make this concrete, can you help us by drafting a mutual action plan that includes the following provisioning items so we can schedule dependencies on our infra side?

- Redwood org invite & test API key (scoped to sandbox)
- IP allowlist for our staging endpoints (we'll provide ranges)
- VPC peering + route table guidance (AWS us-west-2)
- Expected maintenance windows / fallback if peering can't be completed in time
- Success criteria for the evaluation (cost/TPS/latency targets)

We'd like to aim for a 3-week evaluation starting mid-May if the network setup can be completed. Jordan (cc'd) will own the VPC networking on our side and can provide CIDRs.

Also, we'd appreciate a short checklist and a target close timeline we can put into our procurement calendar.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Patel
Director, Data Products | Luma Analytics

Hi Sara — great to hear and thanks for the clear ask. I've pulled together a first-pass Mutual Action Plan and a network configuration template for your networking team. Quick summary below; draft MAP attached for you to review.

High-level MAP (draft):
1) Week 0 (provisioning) — Redwood creates a sandbox org, issues a scoped API key + test token; we'll send invite to the org admin.
2) Week 0-1 (networking) — Luma provides CIDR ranges; we update IP allowlist and coordinate VPC peering.
3) Week 1 (validation) — smoke tests (token auth, small inference runs), sample load test results shared.
4) Week 2 (evaluation) — run representative traffic, collect latency/cost metrics, share dashboard.
5) Week 3 (wrap) — review against success criteria and next steps (dedicated capacity or hosted).

Immediate asks from our side:
- Please share the staging CIDRs Jordan will use and a point of contact for peering (name/email).
- Confirm who will be the org admin to accept the Redwood invite.

Attachments: MAP_Luma_v1.pdf (Mutual Action Plan - draft, 3 pages), network_config_template.xlsx (VPC peering checklist).

I'll let Neha (solutions) chime in on technical constraints (quantization/profile recommendations) and Marissa will lead the timeline/contracting side.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Sara / Jordan — thanks for the CIDRs and the peering window. Below is a concise action checklist we propose; please confirm owners and we'll lock the dates.

POC Provisioning Checklist (owners & target dates):
- Redwood: create Luma sandbox org + invite org admin (RAFAEL) — target 05/12
- Redwood: issue scoped API key (sandbox) + test token; post in secure channel — target 05/12
- Luma: confirm peering acceptance and provision VPC in us-west-2 — target 05/14
- Redwood + Luma networking: peering setup & route table exchange — target 05/15 (09:00-12:00 PT)
- Redwood: update IP allowlist with provided CIDRs — done during peering window
- Redwood: run smoke tests & share results (50 concurrent requests sample) — target 05/16
- Redwood + Luma: execute evaluation traffic (Week of 05/19)
- Success criteria: median latency < 120ms at 95th pct; cost < $0.015 per 1k tokens for the evaluated workload; model output quality threshold (sample prompts to be agreed)

Security & procurement items:
- Rafael will link SOC2 summary and data handling note (for POC scope only).
- Marissa will draft a short statement limiting data retention during POC (30 days) for procurement.

Please confirm the org admin name we should invite and whether the 05/15 peering window is acceptable. Once you confirm, Rafael will upload the final MAP to HubSpot and we'll generate a DocuSign for the standard POC agreement (no-cost evaluation).

Thanks — Marissa Cole
